notes: בֵּין הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְחֹל is read by the connective the ASV actually writes (rule 26): בֵּין takes *between* and the לְ takes *and*, which leaves neither an `added` connective nor an unrepresented preposition.
The possessive חוֹמָה לוֹ clause is verbless, so the לְ carries *had* and its suffix the subject pronoun (rule 43).

The two substantival expressions differ by whether an article morpheme is present: הַקֹּדֶשׁ takes *that which* on its article and heads on *that* (rule 41), while anarthrous חֹל takes *that which was* into its own unit and heads on *common* (rules 46, 20).
